hints: Look closely at the two middle carbon atoms and check if each one is attached to four different groups.
Count every atom carefully from the skeletal structure, remembering that each line end and bend hides carbon and hydrogen atoms.
Think about which OH groups are acidic enough to release $H^+$ in water, carboxylic acid groups versus alcohol groups.
walkthrough:
**Check for chiral centres**

Look at the two central carbons, each is $CH(OH)$. Each is bonded to $H$, $OH$, a $COOH$ group on one side, and a $CH(OH)COOH$ group on the other side.

That is four different groups, so each central carbon is chiral. That gives 2 chiral centres, so statement 1 is correct.

**Work out the molecular formula**

Count the atoms: 4 carbons in the chain, 6 oxygens (2 from each $COOH$ plus 2 from the alcohols), and hydrogens.

$$\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_6$$
For H: 2 from the two $COOH$ groups + 2 from the two $CH$ groups + 2 from the two alcohol $OH$ groups = 6 H in total. So statement 2 which says $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{O}_6$ is incorrect.

**Decide how many $H^+$ are released**

Tartaric acid has four $OH$ groups in total, but only two are part of carboxylic acids ($COOH$).

Only the $COOH$ groups ionise readily in water to give $H^+$. Alcohol $OH$ groups are very weak acids and stay intact. So one molecule gives 2 $H^+$ ions, not 4, so statement 3 is incorrect.

Only statement 1 is correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three statements. Statement 1 is right, but statement 2 has the wrong H count and statement 3 wrongly assumes alcohol groups release $H^+$.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes statement 2. The true formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_6$, not $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{O}_6$. Students often forget the H atoms on the central $CH$ groups when counting.
options.C: Incorrect because both statements 2 and 3 are wrong. Statement 2 miscounts hydrogen, and statement 3 confuses the four $OH$ groups with four acidic protons. Only the two $COOH$ protons are lost.
options.D: Correct because only statement 1 is true. The molecule has two chiral centres, its formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_6$, and it is diprotic (releases 2 $H^+$), not tetraprotic.
